A.explanation: This is the direction of the electric field $E$ at X, tangent to the field line. The force on a negative electron is opposite to $E$.

B.explanation: This points down toward the dipole and is not tangent to the field line through X, so it cannot be the field or force direction.

C.explanation: This also points down toward the dipole and is not tangent to the field line through X, so it cannot be the field or force direction.

D.explanation: The field at X is to the left along the tangent, so $F = qE$ on a negative electron is to the right, opposite to the field.

hints: Look at the field line that passes through point X at the top and find its tangent there - the arrows A and D lie along the tangent.
Recall field lines leave the positive charge and enter the negative charge, so check which way the arrows on that top loop point at X.
Recall force on a charge is $F = qE$ - for an electron $q$ is negative, so the force is opposite to the field direction at X.
walkthrough: Identify point X at the top of the outer loop. The electric field direction at any point is tangent to the field line through that point, so only A or D can be the field direction.
Determine the sense of the field line. Lines start on the + charge on the right and finish on the - charge on the left.
Follow the outer loop on the right side upward to X and then down the left side. At the top point X the motion along the line is toward the left, toward A.
So the electric field $E$ at X is in direction A.
Use $F = qE$ for the electron. The electron charge $q = -e$ is negative, so the force vector is in the opposite direction to $E$.
Opposite to A to the left is to the right. This is option D.
